title: Dedicated throughput indemnity and reconciliation framework for reserved pools
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket defines a reconciliation-first SLA and crediting framework for Dedicated (reserved) GPU pools. The goal is to give customers predictable economic remedies for measurable throughput degradations while preserving operational incentives for Redwood to remediate via autoscale and routing before credits are issued.

Scope:
- Define measurable SLA metrics tailored to reserved pools (bounded-serve-time and sustained-throughput floor).
- Specify a deterministic error-budget consumption model that spans short incident bursts and sustained degradation windows.
- Produce contract-ready clause templates (metrics, notice, credit calculation, exclusions, escalation).
- Define an autoscale "escrow" window and conditional credit reduction for successful failover/autoscale remediation.
- Provide worked examples and sample monthly credit computations for legal/commercial teams.

Proposed metrics (new acronyms introduced intentionally):
1) Bounded Serve Time (BST): percentage of requests that observe server-side token latency <= L for a specified quantile (e.g., 95th percentile) measured over a rolling 1-hour window. BST is computed at the tenant pool level.
2) Sustained Throughput Floor (STF): committed sustained throughput R_committed measured in tokens/sec averaged over 5-minute aligned windows; STF violation occurs when observed throughput median across windows falls below a threshold fraction (e.g., 90%) of R_committed for more than W consecutive windows.
3) Availability of Model Variant (AMV): boolean uptime of the customer's pinned model variant within the pool (for cases where Redwood falls back to compatible variants, this is reported separately).

Error budget and credit model (conceptual):
- Error budget (EB) is defined monthly per customer: EB_month = (1 - SLA_target) * measurement_weighting. Separate EB buckets for BST and STF.
- When a measured violation occurs, compute a degradation score (DS) from severity and duration. DS is normalized to [0,1] per incident.
- Credit calculation: Credit = Monthly_fee * Credit_factor * DS * Exposure_adjustment
  where Credit_factor is a contract-tier scalar (e.g., 0.5 for standard, 1.0 for enterprise), and Exposure_adjustment scales credits by the fraction of minutes the customer's pool was impacted vs total minutes in the month.
- Autoscale escrow: if an autoscale action is triggered by Redwood within Escrow_window (default 10 minutes) and achieves at least 75% of target throughput within Escrow_grace (default 30 minutes), credits for that incident are reduced by Escrow_discount (default 50%). This encourages rapid remediation and aligns incentives.

Sample credit formula (executable text for contracts):
- Let M = monthly committed fee for Dedicated pool. For an incident i with duration d_i minutes affecting fraction f_i of pool capacity and severity s_i (0..1):
  IncidentCredit_i = M * TierScalar * s_i * (d_i / MinutesInMonth) * f_i * (1 - EscrowDiscountIfRemediated)
- Total monthly credit is the sum over incidents, capped at CapPercent * M (default CapPercent = 30%).

Exclusions and force majeure:
- Scheduled maintenance (>=48hr advance notice) and customer-initiated configuration changes excluded.
- Downstream customer code (misuse, excessive prefix patterns) excluded unless Redwood analysis demonstrates service side causation.

Contract language (draft clause for insertion into T&Cs):
"Service Level Commitments: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Dedicated throughput such that the Service meets the Bounded Serve Time (BST) and Sustained Throughput Floor (STF) metrics as defined in Schedule A. If Redwood fails to meet these metrics, Customer may be eligible for a Service Credit as set forth in the Credit Computation Appendix. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for service-level failures. Credits will be computed monthly and applied as a credit against future invoices. Credits are subject to exclusions and caps described below."

Operational telemetry and measurement requirements:
- Metric definitions are to be implemented in the Console reporting surface and the billing pipeline: per-tenant time series for token throughput, per-request server-latency quantiles, and autoscale action logs linked to incident windows.
- Measurement windows must be aligned and reproducible: 60-minute rolling windows for BST reporting, 5-minute aligned windows for STF evaluation.

Deliverables:
- Finalized metric definitions and computation pseudocode for engineering (this ticket).
- Contract clause text (legal), sample SLO dashboard (DX), and example invoices with credits applied (finance).
- Integration tasks for ENG: PR to runtime telemetry + billing connector (ENG-38421), autoscale log tagging (ENG-39210).

Open questions / trade-offs:
1) Quantile selection for BST: 95th vs 99th — 99th penalizes tail latency but may be noisy for short windows. Proposal: default 95th, enterprise opt-in 99th.
2) Escrow window sizing: shorter windows reduce credit liability but require faster autoscale infra; default 10 minute window pending ENG throughput tests.
3) CapPercent: conservative default 30% may be higher for high-touch enterprise deals.
4) Whether credits should be prorated by request-type (chat vs embedding) — initially uniform by token exposure; revisit in Q3 after usage analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract-ready clause drafted and approved by Legal & Revenue Ops.
- ENG PRs opened for telemetry and autoscale log tagging.
- Console draft SLO dashboard showing BST/STF test data.
- Example credit workbook for 3 sample customers (low, medium, high committed spend).

- Billing connector spec (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/dedicated-billing-spec
- Engineering tickets: ENG-38421 (telemetry pipeline), ENG-39210 (autoscale tagging).
